Subject: Request — temporary P1/P2 response-window exception for weekend maintenance

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We have a scheduled infrastructure maintenance this coming weekend (Aug 2–3) that will require full database failover testing and a short application restart window. Our ops leads have proposed a maintenance window 00:00–06:00 PDT (07:00–13:00 UTC) during which we will accept extended vendor response SLAs for routine, non-blocking alerts.

Specifically we are asking Redwood for a temporary exception to our P2 response window (extend to 4 hours from 1 hour) and P1 acknowledgement (extend to 30 minutes from 15 minutes) only for the maintenance hours. We understand critical P1 remediation for production-impacting incidents still needs fast action; this carveout is for non-service-affecting alerts that would otherwise trigger on-call.

Please advise:
- whether Redwood can accept this scoped exception for the two nights (Aug 2 and Aug 3)
- what bridge/on-call coverage you propose to minimize customer impact
- whether Redwood will provide a temporary credit for the reduced SLA guarantees

Attached: Atlas maintenance plan (atlas-maintenance-request.pdf) and our maintenance contact list.

Thanks,
Sofia James
Head of Platform Ops — Atlas Payments

Thanks for the ping — read Atlas's maintenance doc. Suggest the following minimal-risk operational approach we can offer them this week: 

1) Scoped exception window: Aug 2 00:00–06:00 PDT and Aug 3 00:00–06:00 PDT. Exception applies only to non-service-affecting alerts. Any alert that clearly meets P1 definition (customer-impacting major outage) triggers standard P1 workflow.

2) Bridge coverage (recommended):
- Primary bridge owner: Ben Carter (on-call shadow) — ben.carter@redwood.com
- Secondary: Rishi Malhotra (lead on-call) — will be reachable by pager/phone for escalations
- Additional SRE support: assign on-call reserve from the EU team if cross-timezone is required

3) Escalation path (explicit):
- T+0: Notification to bridge (Slack #support-bridge + PagerDuty)
- T+15min: If P1 suspected, primary begins immediate remediation; escalate to secondary if no progress
- T+30min: Executive alert to Laura Bennett and Marissa Cole for customer comms

4) Canary and rollback: we will run a canary checklist at 23:30 PDT before the maintenance window (attached canary-checklist.md). If canary fails, we abort and keep standard SLAs in place.

5) Credit proposal: offer a one-time 10% credit on the next invoice (or equivalent pro-rated credit) in exchange for the scoped exception. This is conservative relative to their request and keeps precedence limited.

6) Runbook & docs: I'll attach a short bridge runbook (sat-bridge-runbook.pdf) with escalation numbers, runbook steps, and the contact list. I'll also file a short Jira ticket to track the exception (SUP-4998).

If everyone agrees, Marissa can communicate the proposal to Atlas and I'll schedule the bridge + create the PagerDuty rotation. Need Laura's explicit sign-off on the credit.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
